meta.status: authored audit; consumed by the P2 scenario builder
rules: Every state in the 1900 catalog (independent, personal union, autonomous vassal, dominion, occupied state) administers its own customs territory unless listed in `unions`.

A dependent territory (colony, protectorate, dependency, autonomous province, self-governing colony) belongs to its sovereign's customs territory unless listed in `territoryExceptions` with a modelled outcome.
Political subordination alone never merges two states' markets; only a recorded customs arrangement does.
meta.confidence: medium: arrangements are well documented; dates and legal details are summarised, not quoted

sources.citation: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 11th edition (1911), articles on Luxemburg, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Norway, Crete, Bulgaria, Egypt, Finland, Newfoundland and Cape Colony.

Clemens, M. A. and Williamson, J. G. (2004). Why did the tariff-growth correlation change after 1950? Journal of Economic Growth 9(1): 5-46 (country tariff series from 1865, including the Latin American states and the British dominions).
Bairoch, P. (1989). European trade policy, 1815-1914. In The Cambridge Economic History of Europe, vol. VIII. Cambridge University Press.

unions.arrangement: Austro-Liechtenstein customs treaty of 1852, in force until 1919
Italo-Sammarinese convention of 1862 placing San Marino in the Italian customs area

ownTerritoryNotes.note: Separate tariff from Sweden after the inter-kingdom trade law (mellomriksloven) lapsed in 1897, despite the personal union.
Autonomous vassal with its own customs administration; duty levels limited by the 1878 Treaty of Berlin.
Autonomous Cretan State from 1898 with its own customs revenue under the High Commissioner.
The six colonies kept separate tariffs until the Commonwealth tariff of 1901; the catalog models one Australian country, so one territory.
Separate Cuban customs tariff under the 1899-1902 United States military government.

territoryExceptions.historical: Own Egyptian customs administration under Ottoman suzerainty and British occupation.
territoryExceptions.modelled: Ottoman customs territory until Egypt is a simulated country.

territoryExceptions.historical: Grand Duchy of Finland kept its own tariff and customs frontier with Russia.
territoryExceptions.modelled: Russian customs territory until Finland is a simulated country.

territoryExceptions.historical: Self-governing Newfoundland set its own tariff.
territoryExceptions.modelled: British customs territory until Newfoundland is a simulated country.

territoryExceptions.historical: Cape Colony set its own tariff and formed the 1889 customs union with the Orange Free State (Natal joined in 1899).
territoryExceptions.modelled: British customs territory; the Orange Free State keeps its own territory until the Cape and Natal are simulated countries.

territoryExceptions.historical: Natal set its own tariff and joined the Cape-Orange Free State customs union in 1899.
territoryExceptions.modelled: British customs territory until Natal is a simulated country.
